steps.text: read the term's live uses before naming it: coherence lexicon review <term>
decide what it is: the project's own concept, an alias of one, a property of one (a field, a column, a unit), or an ordinary programming word that needs no entry
settle a contested term from the project's own history (commit messages, pull request discussion) and record the tie-break with decide

when the history does not settle it, escalate instead of deciding: two live senses that no record separates, the owner's word colliding with a name the lexicon rejected, or any rename, retire, reject or lift of a concept; carry on with the term provisional, and apply only with the human's words
before rejecting a name, count the findings it would create; a word in ordinary use gets a qualifying rename, not a bare rejection
propose, then apply with because and over; a human ruling carries the human's words with --human, and none is ever invented

steps.leaves: 0 rejected names and 0 unknown nouns beyond the baseline

pitfalls: rejecting a bare word turned 227 uses of a language keyword into findings (rt-cdcf2a29)
field and column names were nominated as unknown nouns until they were filed as properties of their concepts (d-3283157b)
identifiers written in backticks in specs were nominated as unknown nouns (d-9e7b9247)
common programming words kept as rejected names made hundreds of findings in ordinary code (d-f77ce193)
the owner's own word for a thing collided with a name the lexicon had rejected for another concept (c-c05b409e)
new nouns were left undeclared because the lexicon was outside the session's scope, where an escalation would have reached the owner (u-de8416b2)

3.because: no term was contested: each name and definition comes from the accepted core-loop spec LP1; item board avoids the board collision as LP1 says

4.because: no escalation needed: only declare and define, no rename, retire, reject or lift
